methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $500K total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Photonium is a pre-seed stage company in Chips & Semiconductors founded by Jennifer Song and Adam Mhatre. The company has raised $500K to date. The comparable universe consists of 11 peers in the semiconductor sector, including 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $500K in total capital raised as a proxy for current value, a standard pre-seed to next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $1.25M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the semiconductor sector—while 11 peers exist in the broader space, none of the narrow stage and tier filters returned the minimum three datapoints needed for reliable median anchoring.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.06M to $1.44M, with a median point of $1.25M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and the absence of direct peer multiples. Key uncertainties include the lack of stage-comparable private company data to validate the 2.5x multiplier against actual pre-seed semiconductor rounds, and the unknown applicability of public semiconductor multiples to an early-stage, unfunded venture. A subsequent funding round or expanded peer dataset would materially improve conviction in this range.
